paragraphs: Swamiji said the entire philosophy of Vedanta is packed into this one short story.

Two birds with golden feathers sat on the same tree. The bird at the top was calm and majestic, completely absorbed in its own glory. The bird lower down was restless, hopping about and eating the tree's fruits, some sweet, some bitter.

Once the lower bird bit into a very bitter fruit. It stopped and looked up at the majestic bird above. But it soon forgot and went back to eating as before. Then another bitter fruit came along, and this time it hopped a few branches higher, closer to the bird at the top.

This kept happening, again and again, until at last the lower bird reached the place of the upper bird and lost itself. All at once it understood that there had never been two birds. It had been that upper bird all along, serene, majestic and full of its own glory.
learn: The bitter experiences of life are not only setbacks; they are often what makes us look up and grow. Each disappointment can bring you a branch closer to your calmer, truer self, if you let it.
